title: Finite completed integral models have internal finite presentations
statement: Let ℓ be prime, let E : Type u be a finite normed Q_ℓ-algebra field [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let T : Scheme u be Noetherian with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write A=O_E, B_T for the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and A_T^c=p_T^*C(-,A) for the internal continuous coefficient ring [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. For any ring-sheaf isomorphism c : B_T ≅ C(|-|, A), let Ψ_c be the inverse completed section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-completed-continuous-module-encoding-universes]. If a sheaf M of B_T-modules has a finite stratification with pro-etale local completed realizations of finitely presented scalar A-modules [def-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-models], then Ψ_c(M) is a constructible internal A_T^c-module: on a finite stratification it admits pro-etale local finite presentations by regular coefficient modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module, def-constructible-stratification]. Torsion scalar models and zero modules are allowed; c need not have a chosen normalization.

proof.text: Choose the stratification and covering sieves in the hypothesis. A finite scalar presentation of each local model is taken to a cokernel presentation by finite free coefficient modules: completed constant realization preserves finite colimits and sends the scalar unit to the regular completed module. The same holds after inverse image to the stratum and localization at a cover object, since both are left adjoints and take regular modules to the corresponding inverse-image regular modules.

Section-action equivalence preserves finite sums and cokernels and identifies the regular modules. It commutes with inverse image and slice restriction: on direct images its underlying abelian sections and restrictions are unchanged, so the left-adjoint comparison is the unique mate of that identity. Continuous chart naturality identifies the coefficient rings on a stratum. Restriction along c preserves all finite presentations because c is a ring isomorphism; no compatibility with the scalar A-structure is needed for finite presentation.

Transport the local model isomorphisms and their presentations through these comparisons. A covering sieve of the terminal site object has a generating pro-etale covering family; the corresponding schemes give the cover in the archived local-finite-presentation predicate. Keep the same finite stratification. The resulting internal module is constructible by definition. Empty strata, the empty base and presentations of zero rank satisfy the same argument.

proof_origin.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), with section-action and slice comparison expanded using Stacks 00YV and 03EK.

theorem continuousIntegralModelEncodingUniverses (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T]
    (c : pbcAdicCompletion T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ≅
      latticeCoefficientSheaf T (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))
    (M : pbcModules T (pbcAdicCompletion T (pbcIntegralDatum l E)))
    (hM : IsIntegralStratifiedFinitelyPresented T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) M) :
    IsConstructibleModuleObject
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousCoefficientRingObj
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) T)
      ((completedContinuousModuleEquivalence l E T c).inverse.obj M)
